matching: Same original three pinned media, tools/native dependency files, ten unchanged product modules, serial new processes, same observation plugin and pytest flags; intended differences are source test patch and explicit/fallback output mode. Checkouts and prospective hashing outside timers.

output_setup_actions.definition: Explicit portable output recipe actions; common media-manifest environment assignment, prepared dependencies and pytest invocation excluded equally. No manual elapsed-time estimate.

artifact_semantics: All seven JSON schemas and deterministic values match across all six samples. Coarse remux container sha256 and source_ref varied. The protocol also excluded timeline_eq, which matched across all six raw records. Raw records preserve every field; original media paths and hashes match.
timing_conclusion: No repeatable speed benefit established by these three pairs. First A was slower; later samples overlap. No project-wide or human-time savings inferred.
timing_limits: Small single-machine, single-session sample; no cache reset or warmup exclusion.
Pytest elapsed is reported to 0.01 seconds and includes plugin/test setup.
Controlled invocation wall includes source/prerequisite verification, interpreter startup and logging; it is not portable pytest workload time.
Same local observer adds temporary-fixture/location-recording overhead to both modes.
Only seven opt-in retained-media cases; no full-suite, packaging or product-performance inference.

final_source_only_modes.interpretation: Mode compatibility observation only; not source-before/after benchmark and not pooled with new samples.

negative_control.interpretation: Reliability evidence only; never a successful timing baseline.
